genZNote: Step two of nitrification: takes the nitrite Nitrosomonas made and finishes the job, oxidizing it to nitrate that plants can actually use.

morphology.motility: Non-motile or motile via a single polar flagellum
morphology.notes: Chemolithoautotroph that oxidizes nitrite (NO2-) to nitrate (NO3-) for energy; reproduces by budding.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil, freshwater, and wastewater treatment systems
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Performs the second step of nitrification alongside ammonia-oxidizers like Nitrosomonas

culture.growthCharacteristics: Very slow-growing obligate chemolithotroph; requires nitrite as sole energy source
culture.colonyMorphology: Rarely characterized by colony morphology; typically studied in liquid culture

identificationClues: Obtains energy by oxidizing nitrite to nitrate — will not grow on standard organic media
Completes the two-step nitrification process started by ammonia-oxidizers such as Nitrosomonas
Very slow growth rate compared to most heterotrophic bacteria, a key reason 'cycling' a new aquarium filter takes weeks
Not associated with human or animal disease

examFacts.importantTest: Obligate growth on nitrite as energy source; nitrate production
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Performs the second step of nitrification (nitrite → nitrate), completing the cycle Nitrosomonas begins
